Plot Bayesian flood quantile curves with PP uncertainty and observations

Source: R/custom_functions.r
fx.plot.quantile.curves.gg.Rd

Produces a hydrology-style return-period plot (log-x) with: scenario-specific posterior quantile curves, pointwise credible intervals, plotting-position uncertainty bars, and observed annual maxima.

Usage

fx.plot.quantile.curves.gg(
  analyses,
  labels = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  T.start = 1.01,
  T.end = 1000,
  plotting.formula = 0.44,
  show.pp.uncertainty = TRUE,
  eps = 1e-30
)

Arguments

analyses

List of analysis objects, one per scenario. Each element must contain at least:

  • ams: numeric vector of annual maxima (or other extremes).

  • is.specific.discharge: logical; TRUE if units are specific discharge (l/km^2/s), FALSE for discharge (m^3/s).

  • any additional components required by quantile.summary().

labels

Optional character vector of scenario labels, same length as analyses. If NULL, labels are generated as "Scenario 1", "Scenario 2", etc.

color

Optional character vector of colors for the scenarios.

T.start

Numeric; minimum return period (years) used for the model curves (on the x-axis, in log scale). Must be strictly greater than 1.

T.end

Numeric; maximum return period (years) used for the model curves (on the x-axis, in log scale).

plotting.formula

Numeric; plotting-position constant \(a\) used to compute empirical return periods for the observed series, via $$p = ((n + 1 - i) - a) / (n + 1 - 2a), \quad T = 1 / (1 - p).$$ Defaults to 0.44 (Gringorten).

show.pp.uncertainty

Logical; if TRUE, plotting-position uncertainty is shown as horizontal segments for each observed value, based on a set of alternative plotting-position constants.

eps

Numeric; small positive value used to clamp plotting probabilities away from 0 and 1 when computing return periods for the uncertainty bars.

Value

A ggplot object representing the return-period plot.
